title: footgun: applyStatePatch on a handler whose class comment and payload name (PATCH_BLUEPRINT, 'patches live entities') imply patching updates component values on existing entities.
detail: For the 'state' component it ADDS only keys the live entity does not already have (line 19: `if (state[key] !== undefined) continue`); a patched value for an EXISTING state key is silently dropped on live entities even though the blueprint definition itself is updated. The test asserts hp stays 10 after a patch to 1 (PatchBlueprintHandler.test.ts:127).

title: footgun: The `total <= 0` guard logs `Transfer failed: target '<id>' at capacity.`, presenting a zero total as a target-capacity condition.
detail: `total` is the sum of `result.clampedPayload`, which calculateTransaction clamps to BOTH target capacity AND source availability (transferLogic.ts clampToAvailable). A total of 0 also occurs when the source has nothing to send, so the 'at capacity' message misattributes a source-empty (or all-non-positive) transfer to the target being full.

title: footgun: clampPayloadToCapacity is named as if it constrains a transfer payload to the target's remaining capacity.
detail: Only positive, finite amounts are clamped; a non-finite or non-positive amount is copied into the output UNCHANGED (lines 53-55), so a negative or NaN transfer amount bypasses capacity clamping entirely and flows downstream.

title: footgun: The `prefix` parameter (default "spawn", e.g. "pending") looks like it namespaces the id counter per prefix.
detail: The serial is shared across all prefixes via the single sys_world.state.spawnSerial counter; the prefix is only a cosmetic label. Two different prefixes never produce the same numeric serial, but the counter does not restart per prefix (documented in the doc comment, contradicting the per-namespace impression the parameter gives).

title: footgun: The comment 'Mutate in-place so concurrent systems in the same tick see the update' plus the enqueued UPDATE_TRAITS_BATCH command frame this as merely enqueuing a state change, and Snapshot.getEntities() is typed ReadonlyArray<Readonly<RuntimeEntity>>.
detail: executeAddTraitAction/executeRemoveTraitAction cast the readonly snapshot entity to a mutable type and directly push/splice context.self.traits (and even assign self.traits=[] when absent), mutating the live entity object during the read-only behavior phase. The Readonly typing is compile-time only; the entity is aliased into the snapshot, so behavior emits a side effect before its command is applied, unlike every other executor which only enqueues.

title: footgun: The name resolveContention and the ContentionRule framing suggest it only reorders transfer requests that compete for the same target resource.
detail: It returns [...otherCommands, ...sortedTransfers], globally hoisting EVERY non-transfer command (KILL, SPAWN, MUTATE-derived, etc.) ahead of ALL transfer commands whenever the batch contains at least one transfer (see caller runtimeCollectCommands.ts line 20). Relative order between a non-transfer command and a transfer that preceded it in emission order is silently inverted.

title: footgun: getAutomationComponent's comment says 'We trust the data is valid because it was validated on Spawn/Input' and returns the raw object typed as AutomationComponent, implying schema invariants (AutomationComponentSchema enforces intervalMs>=1) hold.
detail: It only checks typeof === 'object' and casts via `as any`; no Zod parse runs. Any code path that writes an automation component with intervalMs of 0 (or a non-integer/negative repeats) is accepted, and resolveNextTiming then computes nextRemaining % 0 = NaN before falling back to intervalMs (0).

title: footgun: applyOperator implements '/' as a normal division operator.
detail: Division by zero returns 0 rather than Infinity/NaN, so an expression like `x / y` silently yields 0 when y resolves to 0 instead of surfacing the degenerate case; downstream mutations treat that 0 as a real computed value.

title: footgun: step() reads as a manual single-frame advance (a public sibling of start/stop that pushes the sim forward one step).
detail: It invokes the callback with dt=0. The wired runtime callback (ui/runtime/state/runtimeFactory) forwards that to runtime.tick(0), and advanceRuntimeCoreTick treats dt<=0 as a no-op (normalizeDt(0)=0 -> returns null), so Ticker.step() advances nothing. The real single-step is RuntimeCore.stepOncePreservingPause(), which passes LOGIC_STEP_MS.

title: footgun: The docstring says "Resets ECS + physics state so game.init can re-spawn a fresh world", implying a full clean-slate reset.
detail: It resets tick to 0 but never touches state.status. A runtime that went "fatal" stays fatal across reset(): RuntimeCore.reset() then calls pause(), which is guarded by status !== "fatal" and so no-ops. Only destroy() clears fatal (to "idle"). Reset does not recover a wedged runtime.

title: footgun: advanceRuntimeCoreTick's parameter type RuntimeCoreTickState declares entityStore/systemPhaseBuffers/systemsRegistry as plain `object`, suggesting the type constrains what is passed.
detail: Those fields are immediately cast to `never` before use (core.entityStore as never, etc.), so the declared `object` type provides no checking; the real contract is whatever tickRuntimeCore requires, enforced nowhere at this boundary.

title: footgun: SaveGameState.timeScale:number is a required field, implying the runtime's time scale is captured and restored across a save/load cycle.
detail: The value is never derived from the live runtime and never read on load. serialize() writes a hardcoded 1 (RuntimeSerializer.ts:40) regardless of the actual RuntimeAccessors timeScale, and hydrateRuntime() never restores it. The field is inert on both ends.

title: footgun: SaveGameState.systems.automation:AutomationSnapshot advertises that automation-system state is part of the persisted save and round-trips.
detail: serialize() writes runtime.getAutomationSnapshot() (RuntimeSerializer.ts:44) but the sole load path hydrateRuntime() never calls setAutomationSnapshot, so the snapshot is silently discarded on every load and automation state does not round-trip.

title: footgun: SerializedPhysicsBody.velocity and the code path body.position.x - body.prevPosition.x read as a physical velocity in units per second.
detail: It is a per-tick position delta (Verlet integration), not a units/second velocity; syncPhysicsBody consumes it by reconstructing prevPosition = position - velocity, and it is intentionally never assigned to the body's separate optional velocity field (which the integrator treats as a one-shot units/second seed). Treating this delta as a real velocity elsewhere would be scaled by the tick rate.

title: RESOLVE_TRANSFER credits receiver with no capacity (max) clamp
detail: An existing state entry is incremented by `entry.value += amount` with no reference to `entry.max`. Capacity is only enforced at TRANSFER time (calculateTransaction); if the receiver's max shrinks between initiation and resolution, or for a 'returning' transfer whose source capacity was never checked, resolve overflows the entry above its max. Every other write path (UpdateStateHandler/clampNumeric) clamps to max.

title: Dead unreachable MIN_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD guard
detail: `MIN_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD` is 0 and the preceding guard already returns when `total <= 0`, so `total < MIN_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD` (total < 0) can never be true. The guard is dead code that reads as a configurable minimum-transfer floor but enforces nothing; a future edit to the constant would still be defeated by the `<` (should be `<=`) and the earlier guard.

title: deepMerge of sys_world respawn can accumulate stale array/object state
detail: Re-spawning `sys_world` deep-merges the freshly-built entity into the existing one rather than replacing it. Depending on deepMerge's array/object semantics, previously-accumulated sys_world state (e.g. assignment.assignedIds, serial counters) can persist or blend with blueprint defaults, so a 'respawn to reset' of the world entity does not fully reset it.

title: resolveSpawnOverlap only de-overlaps against the first colliding body
detail: The function returns after resolving the first overlap found in world-iteration order; the pushed-out position is not re-checked against other bodies, so a body spawned into a dense cluster can be relocated onto (still overlapping) a different existing body. Placement quality depends on entity iteration order.

title: AutomationSystem has zero test coverage despite emitting KILL/EXECUTE/UPDATE commands with non-trivial timing math
detail: The repeats-decrement, rollover (nextRemaining % intervalMs), negative-remaining, and repeats===0 kill paths are wired into the runtime tick (RuntimeSystemsRegistry/runtimeSystemPhase) but pinned by no test anywhere in the repo, so a regression in interval/repeat/kill behavior ships undetected.

title: resolveNextTiming decrements repeats by exactly one and enqueues a single EXECUTE regardless of how many intervals a large dt spans
detail: When dt exceeds intervalMs (lag spike, large fixed step, or small interval), the automation fires only once and only loses one repeat that tick; scheduled executions are dropped and the repeat countdown runs slower than wall-clock, diverging from the intended cadence.

title: AutomationSystem contributes soon-to-be-killed automations to the snapshot's nextEventMs/nextCommand
detail: updateSnapshot runs before the repeats===0 kill check, so an automation being killed this tick can still set the reported nextCommand/nextEventMs, making the AutomationSnapshot advertise an event that will never execute.
